articles.full_text:
Maharashtra weather today: Heatwave continues, IMD issues yellow alert for 5 districts
Post-monsoon temperatures remain high across Maharashtra with Ratnagiri recording 38.3 degrees Celsius. Mumbai, Thane, Palghar, Raigad and Ratnagiri are expected to face uncomfortable humidity while Amravati and Akola have also reported temperatures above 38 degrees.
New Delhi: Maharashtra is likely to continue experiencing hot and humid weather on October 13, even as the monsoon has withdrawn from the state. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a yellow alert for hot and humid conditions in five districts along the coast, warning residents to brace for uncomfortable weather.
Palghar, Thane, Mumbai, Raigad and Ratnagiri are expected to experience high humidity and heat. The weather is likely to remain hot across the rest of Maharashtra with mostly clear skies and little relief from the rising temperatures.
The conditions follow the withdrawal of the monsoon from Maharashtra. According to the IMD, the monsoon is expected to withdraw from the remaining parts of the country over the next two to three days. Meanwhile, weather conditions are becoming favourable for the onset of northeast monsoon rainfall over southern peninsular India.
Yellow alert in 5 districts
The IMD has warned of hot and humid conditions in Palghar, Thane, Mumbai, Raigad and Ratnagiri on Tuesday, October 13. The same warning was issued for these districts on Monday, October 12.
The rest of the state is also likely to experience warm conditions with clear skies allowing temperatures to remain high. Residents, particularly those spending long hours outdoors, may find the combination of heat and humidity uncomfortable.
The monsoon withdrawal boundary is currently passing through Kolkata, Angul, Khammam and Honnavar. With the skies clearing after the rainy season, temperatures have continued to rise in several parts of Maharashtra.
Maharashtra temperature update
Temperatures have crossed 35 degrees Celsius in several parts of the state, adding to the discomfort during the post-monsoon period.
According to weather records for the past 24 hours, Ratnagiri recorded Maharashtra’s highest maximum temperature at 38.3 degrees Celsius. Amravati and Akola followed closely with both cities recording maximum temperatures of 38.2 degrees Celsius.
In contrast, the hill station of Mahabaleshwar recorded the state’s lowest minimum temperature at 18 degrees Celsius, offering relatively cooler conditions.
With hot and humid weather expected to persist in the five coastal districts, residents are advised to stay hydrated, limit prolonged exposure to the sun and take precautions during the hottest parts of the day.
